ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: A benzene ring is visible in the figure, and an NH2 substituent is connected at the ortho position of the benzene ring; the benzene ring is also connected to an alkene fragment. The carbon on the right side of the alkene is connected to an R substituent and is connected to the adjacent carbon below; this lower carbon is connected to R1 and forms a carbonyl-related transition-state representation with an oxygen atom. There are curved arrows in the figure, but the question requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning: After ignoring the arrows, the skeleton can be read as an ortho-aminophenyl connected to an alkene carbon, the other end of the alkene connected to a carbon bearing a wildcard substituent, and continuing to the carbonyl carbon; the carbonyl carbon additionally bears a wildcard substituent. According to the specified method, starting from the wildcard at the carbonyl end is written as *C(=O), continuing to the alkene part is /C(*)=C\, and then attaching the ortho-aminobenzene ring c1ccccc1N gives the SMILES: *C(=O)/C(*)=C\c1ccccc1N.

method.method_draft: First describe the visible skeleton: an ortho-NH2 substituted phenyl group is bonded to an alkene carbon; that alkene is bonded to a carbon bearing a wildcard R substituent and connected to a carbonyl carbon bearing another wildcard substituent. Ignore all curved arrows in the transition-state drawing. Convert this connectivity to a SMILES fragment by starting at the carbonyl substituent wildcard, writing *C(=O), then continuing to the alkene carbon as /C(*)=C\, then appending the ortho-aminophenyl ring as c1ccccc1N. This yields *C(=O)/C(*)=C\c1ccccc1N.

Identify an ortho-aminophenyl ring attached through an exocyclic C=C to an alpha-substituted carbon next to a carbonyl; the carbonyl carbon bears one generic R/R1 substituent and the alpha alkene carbon bears another generic R substituent. planner_metadata.text_role: Use the prompt instruction that the required output is the SMILES expression of the shown transition-state structure and that arrows should be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use SMILES conventions: aromatic benzene with ortho amino is written as c1ccccc1N when entered from the side-chain attachment atom; generic R groups are represented by wildcard atoms '*'; carbonyl is C(=O); alkene stereochemistry is encoded with slash/backslash around the C=C according to the drawing.
